radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate mpMRI | Date: 15 Dec 2024 | Amsterdam UMC, AMC Campus
Referral rationale centers on a PSA reading of 6.5 ng/mL alongside a palpable nodule on DRE and a previously negative biopsy sample.

FINDINGS:
Total glandular size measures 42.0 mL. Zonal architecture remains standard without midline hypoplasia. A discrete focus occupies the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland level, spanning roughly 14 × 11 × 10 mm. T2 sequences show hypointensity with poorly demarcated borders. DWI highlights pronounced diffusion restriction paired with depressed ADC values. DCE imaging captures early, focal uptake compared to adjacent tissue. Extracapsular spread, seminal vesicle involvement, suspicious lymph nodes, and bone metastases are absent.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 classification applied to the right peripheral zone mid-gland focus.
Prostate volume 42.0 mL, PSAD 0.15 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.59320194.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Serial measurements show progression from 3.7 ng/mL to 4.2 ng/mL. The gentleman reports zero lower urinary tract symptoms, registering an IPSS of 0/35. Following the established upward trend and his previous negative biopsy outcome, urology consultation for advanced imaging and possible re-sampling was scheduled.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Early screening flagged a PSA level of 2.1 ng/mL. A follow-up draw three months later recorded a rise to 3.2 ng/mL. No haematuria or urinary complaints are reported by the patient. Urology evaluation was consequently triggered to conduct a full assessment.
